headline: Q1 and Q2 FY2027 show revenue growth above 85% and gross margin near 75%, while net cash fell to $24.1bn as debt and receivables rose.
summary: NVIDIA's first two quarters of fiscal 2027 kept the growth and margin theses intact. Q1 revenue was $81.6bn, up 85% year over year, and Data Center revenue was $75.2bn, up 92% [2]. Gross margin was 74.9% in Q1 and 75.0% in Q2, against 60.5% and 72.4% a year earlier, so the 72% signpost in the thesis is already met [2][3]. Consensus FY2027 EPS of $9.67 is up 4.0% over 90 days, and FY2028 EPS of $16.61 is up 27.7% [3]. The weaker item is the balance sheet. Net cash fell from $68.2bn in Q1 to $24.1bn in Q2, total debt rose to $38.4bn from $11.0bn at year-end, and Q2 free cash flow margin was 22.2% against 28.8% a year earlier [2][3]. Net cash is still positive, so the invalidation test has not been triggered, but the new guarantees and supply commitments raise the stakes. Supply and capacity commitments rose from $119bn to $279bn in one quarter [2]. Sources: [1] releases unavailable, [2] 10-Qs, [3] Yahoo Finance, [4] annual report and thesis log.
results_commentary:
Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended April 2026): revenue was $81.6bn, up 85% year over year and 20% sequentially [2]. Data Center revenue was $75.2bn, up 92% year over year, driven by the Blackwell 300 ramp and InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet and NVLink demand [2]. Hyperscalers stayed at about 50% of Data Center revenue. The China shock showed up in the mix rather than the total: no Hopper Data Center shipments went to China, against $4.6bn in the year-ago quarter [2]. Edge Computing rose 29% to $6.4bn, but consumer PC demand was slower because of higher memory and system prices, a named cause [2]. Gross margin was 74.9% against 60.5%, helped by the absence of the prior year's $4.5bn H20 charge and lower inventory provisions [2]. GAAP diluted EPS was $2.39 against $0.76 [2]. Yahoo's normalized Q1 EPS of $1.87 is on a different basis and is not comparable with the GAAP figure [3].

Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 2026): the scorecard shows total revenue up 105.9% year over year, the fastest growth in the period, with gross margin at 75.0% against 72.4% and operating margin at 66.2% against 60.8% [3]. Operating expenses fell to 8.7% of revenue from 11.6%, so the margin gain came from scale rather than cost cuts alone [3]. Q2 diluted EPS was $2.46 [3]. The Q2 Data Center segment table was not in the text retrieved, so Data Center growth for Q2 is not verified here; total revenue growth is the only Q2 growth figure available. Several measures weakened. Free cash flow margin fell to 22.2% from 28.8% [3]. Days sales outstanding rose to 60 from 54 a year earlier and 45 in Q1 [3]. Net cash fell to $24.1bn from $43.4bn a year earlier and $68.2bn in Q1, as total debt rose to $38.4bn from $11.0bn at FY2026 year-end [2][3]. The 10-Q links the timing of operating cash flow to extended payment terms for investment-grade customers on large multi-quarter agreements [2]. The filings retrieved do not split the net cash decline by cause, so the relative weight of receivables, investments and debt is not established. Share count fell 0.8% year over year to 24.15bn [3].

Trend across the two quarters: revenue and margins held or accelerated; cash conversion and balance sheet liquidity deteriorated. Q2 supply and capacity commitments rose to $279bn from $119bn in the prior quarter, and equity investments reached $99bn with $25bn of further commitments [2]. Q1 and Q2 quarterly figures for revenue and Data Center are only partly available: the Q2 revenue value and the Q1 year-ago net cash were not in the retrieved text, so they are not shown.

thesis_check.thesis: T1: Data center demand keeps NVIDIA's growth well above peers through fiscal 2027.
thesis_check.signpost: Data Center revenue growth above 50% year over year in each FY2027 quarter reported, and Rubin production shipments starting in the second half of FY2027 [1][3].
thesis_check.evidence: Q1 Data Center revenue was $75.2bn, up 92% year over year [2], well above the 50% signpost. For Q2, total revenue rose 105.9% year over year [3]; the Q2 Data Center segment figure was not in the retrieved text, so it is not verified. The Q2 10-Q states Vera Rubin began production shipments in Q3 FY2027, which is inside H2 FY2027 as the signpost requires [2].

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Gross margin recovers above 72% as Blackwell yields mature and the H20 charge does not recur.
thesis_check.signpost: Quarterly gross margin back above 72% by the end of FY2027 (January 2027) [1].
thesis_check.evidence: Gross margin was 74.9% in Q1 against 60.5% a year earlier, with the prior-year $4.5bn H20 charge not recurring [2]. Q2 gross margin was 75.0% against 72.4% a year earlier [3], so the 72% signpost has been met in both quarters. Held, not extended: Q2 was flat on Q1, so the trend is stable rather than rising.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: The stock is priced for a steep growth fade, so returns depend on consensus EPS being delivered.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2027 EPS at or above the $9.67 consensus, and the FY2028 EPS estimate holding above $16 through the FY2027 year-end [3].
thesis_check.evidence: FY2027 EPS consensus is $9.67, up 4.0% from $9.30 90 days ago, and FY2028 consensus is $16.61, up 27.7% from $13.00 over 90 days, with 7 upward and 0 downward revisions in the last 30 days [3]. Reverse DCF growth is 25.6% against the invalidation level of growth above 30% [4], and the current EV is $3.54tn [3]. Illustrative only: at the FY2028 consensus EPS, the forward P/E is 9.0x at $149.30 [3]. FY2028 consensus range is wide, from $12.27 to $18.79 [3].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Free cash flow and net cash can absorb the China and customer shocks without strain.
thesis_check.signpost: Net cash stays positive in each FY2027 quarter, and any H200 revenue is disclosed in the first half of FY2027 [1][2].
thesis_check.evidence: Net cash was $68.2bn in Q1 and $24.1bn in Q2, still positive [2][3]. Net cash fell from $43.4bn a year earlier to $24.1bn in Q2, and total debt rose to $38.4bn from $11.0bn at year-end [2][3]. Q2 free cash flow margin was 22.2% against 28.8%, and days sales outstanding rose to 60 from 54 [3]. The Q1 10-Q says no H200 revenue had been generated yet [2]; the Q2 H200 disclosure was not in the retrieved text. The China Hopper shipments were zero in Q1 [2].

risk_update: Materialised or intensified: counterparty and commitment exposure rose sharply. Supply and capacity commitments went from $119bn in Q1 to $279bn at July 26, 2026 [2]. In August 2026 NVIDIA guaranteed lease obligations for the SB Energy PORTS campus, capped at $105bn, to host compute for OpenAI under 20-year leases, with exposure starting in FY2029 [2]. A separate $36bn of AI cloud commitments carries a purchase obligation if the AI clouds cannot resell capacity [2]. Eased or unchanged: China produced no Hopper Data Center revenue in Q1 and no H200 revenue had been generated by the Q1 10-Q [2]; the Q2 H200 disclosure was not in the retrieved text. New: the Q2 10-Q lists investigations and information requests from regulators in the EU, US, UK, China and South Korea, and a French inquiry into whether gaming and data center GPUs are separate product categories [2]. Supply constraints are now stated explicitly as current [2]. The Q2 10-Q also notes that Rubin has started production shipments, which moves product-transition risk from forecast to execution.
outlook: Consensus, retrieved 26 November 2026 after the 10-K, expects FY2027 revenue of $423.8bn (+96%) and EPS of $9.67, and FY2028 EPS of $16.61 [3]. Revisions are upward: FY2027 EPS is up 4.0% over 90 days and FY2028 EPS up 27.7% [3]. The FY2028 range is wide, $12.27 to $18.79 [3]. Yahoo also shows a quarter ending 31 October 2026 with EPS of $2.68 against a $2.47 estimate; no release or 10-Q for that quarter was in the pack, so it is not scored [3]. Watch: Data Center growth in the Q3 and Q4 FY2027 filings; whether H200 revenue is disclosed; net cash staying positive; days sales outstanding; and the SB Energy and AI cloud commitments. Invalidation points from the annual report [4]: Data Center growth under 25%, FY2027 EPS consensus below the $9.05 level from 90 days earlier, gross margin under 70%, or net cash turning negative.
